cases.purpose: With the weak crypto reference reading as unresolved (zero stored by a parent process into the running candidate), send-secret fails with status 1 and the documented diagnostic for valid and invalid handles, writes nothing to the descriptor, while bad-fd and usage errors keep their own statuses; before the store the same requests take the crypto path.
cases.oracle: expect.c declares bashcrypto_secret_write_fd weak and refuses send-secret with 'send-secret requires crypto secret handle support' when the reference is null, before any handle is looked up. The null state is produced exactly as a linker or loader leaves an unresolved weak symbol (zero in its slot), applied by an independent parent process to the running candidate; the same request before the store, with a valid and an invalid handle, is the control that the crypto path is otherwise live.
cases.comparison: Exact expectation for status and output derived independently of the candidate; raw stdout, stderr and fixture files are retained as diagnostics.

files.cand.sh:
[[ $(type -t expect) == builtin && $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]] || exit 99
printf 'w5-secret-bytes\n' > pw
crypto secret-read -h H < pw
exec 5>fdout
expect send-secret 5 "$H" 2>err; echo "before: valid rc=$? written=$(/usr/bin/wc -c < fdout) err=[$(< err)]"
expect send-secret 5 no-such-handle 2>err; echo "before: invalid rc=$? err=[$(< err)]"
: > fdout
echo READY
read -r go
expect send-secret 5 "$H" 2>err; echo "after: valid rc=$? written=$(/usr/bin/wc -c < fdout) err=[$(< err)]"
expect send-secret 5 no-such-handle 2>err; echo "after: invalid rc=$? written=$(/usr/bin/wc -c < fdout) err=[$(< err)]"
expect send-secret x "$H" 2>err; echo "after: bad-fd rc=$? err=[$(< err)]"
expect send-secret 5 2>err; echo "after: usage rc=$? err=[$(< err)]"

cases.script:
guard_guest() {
  local token vendor virt inside outside length extra
  local -a uid_rows
  [[ -r /etc/bashos-parity-vm && -r /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || return 125
  IFS= read -r token </etc/bashos-parity-vm || return 125
  IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || return 125
  [[ $vendor == QEMU && $token =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || return 125
  (( UID == EUID )) || return 125
  if (( EUID == 0 )); then
    mapfile -t uid_rows </proc/self/uid_map || return 125
    (( ${#uid_rows[@]} == 1 )) || return 125
    read -r inside outside length extra <<<"${uid_rows[0]}" || return 125
    [[ $inside == 0 && $outside == 2000 && $length == 1 && -z $extra ]] || return 125
  else
    (( EUID == 2000 )) || return 125
  fi
  virt=$(/usr/bin/systemd-detect-virt --vm) || return 125
  [[ $virt == qemu || $virt == kvm ]] || return 125
}
guard_guest || { printf 'refusing non-fixture guest\n' >&2; exit 125; }
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w5-weaksym.py "$BASH" "$PWD/cand.sh"
echo "helper rc=$?"
cases.stdout:
before: valid rc=0 written=15 err=[]
before: invalid rc=1 err=[/tmp/parity-case/cand.sh: line 6: expect: secret-write-fd: invalid handle]
READY
weaksym: slot-found=1 before=resolved after=null
after: valid rc=1 written=0 err=[/tmp/parity-case/cand.sh: line 10: expect: send-secret requires crypto secret handle support]
after: invalid rc=1 written=0 err=[/tmp/parity-case/cand.sh: line 11: expect: send-secret requires crypto secret handle support]
after: bad-fd rc=2 err=[/tmp/parity-case/cand.sh: line 12: expect: bad fd: x]
after: usage rc=2 err=[/tmp/parity-case/cand.sh: line 13: expect: send-secret needs FD HANDLE]
helper rc=0
